Usage: drive record goal <session> <text> ... [flags]

Record what a session sets out to do, in plain terms for the owner.

Give a goal to a session that has none, which status names (it joined the
batch on a send, or opened without --goal), and replace one once the
session's purpose or scope changes. read and the owner's page show the
latest.

Arguments:
  <session>           The session, by its label in the batch; a closed one too.
  <text> ...          What it sets out to do, in plain terms for the owner: one short paragraph, at
                      most 600 bytes.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help          Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME    Act in this batch instead of the current one, which stays current. It may
                      stand anywhere on the line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
